tasks.title: Cities not given
tasks.statement: Some customers have no city filled in (NULL). Output their name: the condition city IS NULL.
tasks.hint: Compare with NULL using the words IS NULL, not the = sign.

tasks.title: Email given
tasks.statement: Output the name and email of customers who have an email given (IS NOT NULL).

tasks.title: The = NULL trap
tasks.statement: The condition city = NULL is never true. Output the number of customers found by the condition city = NULL, as n (you will get 0).
tasks.hint: A comparison with NULL gives 'unknown', not 'true'.

tasks.title: COUNT(*) and COUNT(column)
tasks.statement: In one row, output: all_rows is the number of rows in customers, with_city is the number of customers with a city filled in, with_email is those with an email filled in.

tasks.title: City but no email
tasks.statement: Output the name of customers who have a city given but no email (city IS NOT NULL AND email IS NULL).

tasks.title: Something is not filled in
tasks.statement: Output the name of customers who have no city or no email filled in.

tasks.title: Brand unknown
tasks.statement: Output the title of products without a brand (brand IS NULL).

tasks.title: Replacing a gap
tasks.statement: Output the customer's name and city; if the city is not given, substitute 'not specified' (COALESCE). Columns name, city.
tasks.hint: COALESCE(a, b, ...) returns the first non-empty value.

tasks.title: Replacing the email
tasks.statement: Output name and email, substituting `'no email'` for NULL.

tasks.title: IFNULL
tasks.statement: IFNULL has two arguments: it is the short form of COALESCE. Output name and IFNULL(city, `'—'`) as city.

tasks.title: First non-empty
tasks.statement: Output name and the first non-empty of email, city, `'empty'` (COALESCE with three arguments) as contact.

tasks.title: Concatenation with NULL
tasks.statement: Concatenation || with NULL gives NULL. Output name || `' — '` || city as label for all customers (those with no city get NULL).
tasks.hint: Any operation with NULL gives NULL.

tasks.title: Concatenation with COALESCE
tasks.statement: Output name || `', '` || COALESCE(city, `'city unknown'`) as label for all customers.

tasks.title: Division by zero
tasks.statement: In SQLite, division by zero gives NULL. Output title and price / stock as ratio (integer division) for all products; where stock = 0, it will be NULL.

tasks.title: NULLIF
tasks.statement: NULLIF(a, b) returns NULL if a = b. Output title and price / NULLIF(stock, 0) as ratio.

tasks.title: Arithmetic with NULL
tasks.statement: Output the results of 1 + NULL, NULL * 5, NULL || 'a' under the names a, b, c: all of them NULL.

tasks.title: NULL = NULL
tasks.statement: Output NULL = NULL as eq, NULL IS NULL as is_null, 1 IS NOT NULL as not_null.

tasks.title: Three-valued logic
tasks.statement: Output NULL AND 0 as a, NULL OR 1 as b, NULL AND 1 as c. Think ahead: the results are 0, 1, NULL.
tasks.hint: 0 AND anything = 0; 1 OR anything = 1; otherwise unknown.

tasks.title: Not Moscow, and NULL too
tasks.statement: The condition city <> `'Moscow'` drops customers with no city. Output the name of everyone whose city is not `'Moscow'`, including those whose city is unknown.

tasks.title: IS NOT, a safe comparison
tasks.statement: In SQLite, the IS NOT operator works as 'not equal' and takes NULL into account. Output the name of customers whose city IS NOT `'Moscow'`.

tasks.title: DISTINCT and NULL
tasks.statement: Output the distinct values of city (NULL counts as one value), in ascending order.

tasks.title: Names starting with A
tasks.statement: Output the name of customers that start with the letter «A» (`LIKE 'A%'`).

tasks.title: Surnames ending in -ov
tasks.statement: Output the name of customers whose surname ends in «ov» (`LIKE '%ov'`).

tasks.title: Gmail
tasks.statement: Output the name and email of customers with an address at gmail.com.

tasks.title: Long names
tasks.statement: Output the name and length(name) as len of customers whose name is longer than 13 characters; ordered by len and name.

tasks.title: Uppercase
tasks.statement: Output the email in uppercase (upper), only the non-empty ones. upper() works for Latin letters.

tasks.title: Lowercase
tasks.statement: Output the distinct brands in lowercase (lower), without NULL.

tasks.title: Trimming spaces
tasks.statement: Output trim(`'  hello  '`) as t, ltrim(`'  hello  '`) as l, rtrim(`'  hello  '`) as r.

tasks.title: Substring
tasks.statement: Output brand and its first three characters substr(brand, 1, 3) as short for products with a known brand; ordered by brand, short, without repeats.

tasks.title: Replacing text
tasks.statement: Output the title of products, replacing the word «Book» with «Textbook» (replace). Only the titles where the word occurs.

tasks.title: Position of a character
tasks.statement: Output email and the position of the @ character (instr) as pos for customers with an email; ordered by email.

tasks.title: Email domain
tasks.statement: Output the distinct email domains (the part after @) as domain: substr(email, instr(email, '@') + 1); ordered by domain.

tasks.title: Number to text
tasks.statement: Output `'Order №'` || id as label for the first five orders (by id).

tasks.title: Customer code
tasks.statement: Output a customer code like C-001 using printf('C-%03d', id) as code, and name; ordered by id, the first 4.

tasks.title: Text and numbers
tasks.statement: Compare strings and numbers: '10' < '9' as text_cmp and 10 < 9 as num_cmp. Strings are compared character by character.

tasks.title: GLOB
tasks.statement: GLOB is like LIKE, but case matters and it uses * and ?. Output the name of customers whose city starts with `'M'` (`city GLOB 'M*'`).

tasks.title: HR: no phone
tasks.statement: HR database. Output the name of employees without a phone (phone IS NULL); ordered by name.

tasks.title: HR: contact
tasks.statement: HR database. Output name and COALESCE(phone, email) as contact for everyone; ordered by id.

tasks.title: HR: no department
tasks.statement: HR database. Output the name of employees without a department (dept_id IS NULL).

tasks.title: HR: no manager
tasks.statement: HR database. How many employees have no manager (boss_id IS NULL)? Column n.

tasks.title: School: no grades
tasks.statement: School database. Output student_id and course_id of the 2024 records where the grade has not been given yet (score IS NULL); ordered by student_id.

tasks.title: Movies without a rating
tasks.statement: Movies database. Output the title of movies that have no rating or no director (rating IS NULL OR director_id IS NULL).
